{
  "jobspec": "#!/bin/bash
#flux: -N 1
#flux: --time-limit=48h

# Note: PBS -q directive (windfall) does not have a direct Flux equivalent.
# Performance consideration: Queue selection not preserved. Job may run on different queue/priority.
# Note: PBS -l select requests 1 node with 28 cores, 168gb memory, 6gb per core, 1 GPU, and os7=True.
# Flux equivalent uses -N for nodes. You may need to specify cores and GPU at submission time.
# Performance consideration: Core count (28) not specified in batch script.
# Note: PBS -l mem and pcmem directives do not have direct Flux equivalents.
# Performance consideration: Memory limits (168gb total, 6gb per core) not enforced. Job may be killed if exceeding node memory.
# Note: PBS ngpus=1 does not translate to Flux batch script directives.
# You may need to use 'flux mini submit -g 1' at submission time.
# Performance consideration: GPU allocation not specified in batch script. Job may not have access to GPUs.
# Note: PBS os7=True constraint does not have a direct Flux equivalent.
# Performance consideration: OS version constraint not preserved.
# Note: PBS -W group_list directive (msurdeanu) does not have a direct Flux equivalent.
# Performance consideration: Group/project association not preserved.
# Note: PBS -j oe (join stdout/stderr) is default behavior in Flux.

cd /xdisk/msurdeanu/mithunpaul/
module load cuda90/neuralnet/7/7.3.1.20
module load python/3.6/3.6.5

#uncomment this if you don't want to reinstall venv- usually you just have to do this only once ever
rm -rf sandeep_bert_venv
mkdir sandeep_bert_venv
python3 -m venv sandeep_bert_venv

#this is the only line you need if you already have a virtual_env set up
source sandeep_bert_venv/bin/activate

cd /xdisk/msurdeanu/mithunpaul/bert_tensorflow

pip install --upgrade pip
#pip install torch==1.5.0+cu92 torchvision==0.6.0+cu92 -f https://download.pytorch.org/whl/torch_stable.html
pip install -r requirements.txt




#####my code part
export PYTHONPATH="/home/u11/mithunpaul/sandeep_bert/"





bash run_sandeep_code.sh
"
}
